q: Does my company need an SBTi FLAG target?
title: Do I need an SBTi FLAG target?
short: You need an SBTi FLAG target if your company is in a sector the SBTi designates as FLAG, such as agricultural production, food processing, or forest and paper products, or if land-related emissions are 20% or more of your total emissions across scopes. Either trigger also requires a no-deforestation commitment.
audience: Indian food, tea, spice, cotton and timber exporters setting SBTi targets

ol: Sector: the SBTi lists FLAG-designated sectors, including forest and paper products, agricultural production, animal-source food production, food and beverage processing, food and staples retailing, and tobacco. A tea estate, spice processor or timber mill usually falls in one of these.
Share: if you are not in a designated sector, add up your FLAG emissions. If they are 20% or more of total Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, a FLAG target is required.

ul: Land use change, such as clearing forest or grassland for farms, in your operations or supply chain.
Land management: fertiliser nitrous oxide, rice methane, enteric methane from cattle, manure, and on-farm machinery.
Removals and storage, such as trees on your land, reported separately and not netted off.
For a buyer of farm goods, most of this sits in Scope 3 Category 1, in the crops and fibre you purchase.

p: A FLAG target is set separately from your energy and industry target, using the SBTi FLAG pathway. It comes with a public commitment to no deforestation across your operations and supply chain. Your non-FLAG target still covers fuel, electricity and other emissions.

Check how the SME route treats FLAG companies on the SBTi site before you apply; the SME route has its own rules and has changed over time. If you cannot apply as an SME, the full corporate route applies.

example.title: Example: cotton yarn exporter, not a designated sector
lines: Total emissions, all scopes: 10,000 t CO2e
FLAG emissions in purchased raw cotton (fertiliser, field operations, land use change): 2,500 t CO2e
25% is above the 20% threshold, so a FLAG target is required alongside the energy and industry target
example.note: Figures are illustrative. The FLAG share depends on the cotton emission factor you use; state its source.

senseible: Senseible measures operational Scope 1 and 2 from your invoices and bills and keeps Scope 3 supplier evidence, which gives you the totals for the 20% test. It does not set or validate SBTi targets.
